A1.justification: Despite the title change, both PDFs describe the same PAR/APE survey. Their text, figures, tables, mathematical notation and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated tables.

before.justification: v1 reviews existing methods, datasets and findings. Neither the main text nor Appendices A-F report original empirical results produced by this work.

after.justification: The new appendices synthesize prior research, and the final performance table compiles outcomes attributed to existing systems. No original experiment or empirical data analysis is reported.

M1.justification: The PAR decomposition and methodological categories remain unchanged. Added descriptions of other systems and practical design recommendations do not introduce an algorithm or model developed by this work.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. The relocated dataset catalog, removal of duplicate entries, and newly reviewed benchmarks such as FlowVerse extend survey documentation rather than experimental coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates comparators against a proposed method. The additional systems in the final performance table are literature comparisons, not an experimentally evaluated baseline set.

E3.justification: The APE hierarchy remains unchanged. Newly discussed benchmark variants and metrics describe prior studies; no evaluation protocol used by this work is added or revised.

E4.justification: The existing robustness-benchmark overview is retained. Appendix I adds an interpretive synthesis of published failure patterns, without introducing an ablation, robustness experiment or empirical case study.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new performance compilation supplies point estimates; Appendix G describes existing robustness metrics.

E6.justification: v3 adds a substantial quantitative literature-results compilation absent from v1: Table 2 on page 23 reports, for example, Inter-GPS at 78.3% on Geometry3K and GPT-4V at 49.9% on MathVista test. These are newly summarized prior-work outcomes under their reported settings, not performance gains from experiments conducted by this survey.

T1.justification: The perception mapping and task formulations in Section 2 are retained. The new appendices add conceptual discussion without new mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The four organizing questions, PAR framework, APE hierarchy and claimed first process-level synthesis remain substantively unchanged. The new title explicitly identifies the work as a survey without changing these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendices G-I substantially expand interpretation: they connect benchmark design to modeling choices, recommend configurations for different application requirements, and organize practical failures across PAR stages. Dataset classifications also change, including PGPS9K from Perception + Alignment to All stages.

D1.justification: v3 adds a first-page link to the companion Awesome Multimodal Mathematical Reasoning GitHub collection. This supplies resource-access information, without adding implementation or reproduction instructions for an original model.

R1.justification: v3 adds source references for previously listed datasets such as UniGeo, TabFact and DUDE, and extends discussion to MathFlow/FlowVerse, DVLR and additional systems in the performance table. Its comparison with prior surveys and process-centric novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and related-work terminology are edited to describe the paper explicitly as a survey. Appendices G-I extend the structure, while the existing main sections and Appendices A-F remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Dataset Table A1 moves into the main text as Table 2, gains citations and loses duplicate rows. A dense performance table is added on page 23, while both figures retain their designs. Appendix table numbering now reuses the main-text labels Table 1 and Table 2.

improvement.justification: Appendices G-I make the survey more useful through concrete design tradeoffs and failure-mode synthesis, while added dataset citations improve traceability. These gains are limited by the new performance table's missing row-level sources and very small type, plus duplicated table numbers. The additions support a modest net improvement despite those presentation and sourcing weaknesses.
